parts:
Hello,

I think you can't because the browser need to know where to connect if you don't say the port, it'll try 80 and if Shiny is not set on port 80 well they won't be able to make a link. Except if you use the 'site_dir' mode 

Here if you want more info => http://rstudio.github.io/shiny-server/latest/#default-configuration

messages.author: bbc57ffa8a14ad13
messages.subject: Re: Gow to set my shinyApp url without port number?
parts:
Aurelien is correct. If your port 80 is already occupied, you won't be able to run Shiny Server on port 80 which means your users will need to specify a port number.

The one exception would be if you're willing to setup an HTTP proxy like Apache or nginx. One of those systems could selectively forward certain traffic from port 80 (for instance, traffic prefaced with "/shiny") to Shiny Server.

Jeff
